body: Hmm, I will take a look. The `RouteBuilder` and `BuilderSupport` have ~ 100 methods which should not be a problem.

FTR `MyBuilder` has no associated interceptors so you can set `quarkus.arc.dev-mode.monitoring-enabled=false` to avoid this particular problem in the dev mode. Of course, this would not help once you add any other interceptor binding to the bean.

Ah, in fact `MyBuilder` also `implements EndpointBuilderFactory` that extends over 300 interfaces with default methods which are also intercepted. So in the end, we need to initialize intercepted metadata for more than 1000 methods in the constructor of the `MyBuilder_Subclass` and that seems to be the current limit. We'll need to split the logic in the constructor, i.e. something similar to what we do for the generated `ComponentsProvider`.

CC @Ladicek @manovotn
Will take a look next week, prob on Mon.
I've mentioned this before but I'll bring it up again: should we flip the default for `quarkus.arc.dev-mode.monitoring-enabled`?

> I've mentioned this before but I'll bring it up again: should we flip the default for `quarkus.arc.dev-mode.monitoring-enabled`?

That's a way how to mitigate the problem, not a way to fix the problem. Any interceptor binding (`@Transactional`, `@ActivateRequestContext`, `@CacheResult`, `@Retry`...) added to the bean would break it anyway.

That said, I've been thinking about `quarkus.arc.dev-mode.monitoring-enabled=false` as well and I think that it's probably a reasonable idea. @Ladicek @manovotn WDYT?
I know it's not a real fix, but the feature does seem to exacerbate issues which is why I am proposing to have it off be default
OTOH it helped us to spot some annoying bugs earlier. Anyway, here we go: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/28940
